title: Guardrails and red-team suite for untrusted tool and news text
why: Layered input and output guards around an LLM agent, tested with a red-team set, are standard for production agents (docs/SOURCES.md, lab sources).
notes: Detection means the guard flagged the text (injection pattern, markup, link, code fence or length); an instruction-like text is replaced before it reaches the model.
The evasion category (paraphrase, spacing, other languages, base64) is expected to get past the regex guards; its misses are the honest limit of this layer.
Report-only: the live agent is unchanged (its defences are the data labelling and the harness limits).
limits: Synthetic attacks written by the project; a determined attacker is not bounded by them. The patterns were refined once after a first run on this same set (three misses and one false positive), so the detection rate is optimistic.
Regex guards cannot understand meaning; a classifier or a second model would be the next layer.
No model was attacked here, so this measures detection, not attack success against an LLM.
